1: Rulers are told to seek God with a sincere heart. Wisdom will not enter a deceitful soul. God did not make death and takes no pleasure in the destruction of the living.
Death entered through sin; God made us for life.
2: The godless say life is short and ends in nothing, so enjoy it and crush the weak. They plot against the just man who calls God his father: "Let us condemn him to a shameful death."
The Church reads this as a prophecy of Christ's Passion.
3: "The souls of the just are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them." They seemed to die, but they are at peace.
Read at funerals. Death is not the end for those who are God's.
4: Better childless with virtue than many wicked children. The just man who dies young is at rest: he was taken so that evil would not corrupt him.
A long life is not the measure of a good one.
5: At the judgement the wicked will see the just man they mocked and say, "We fools! How he is numbered among the sons of God!"
Everything will look different at the end.
6: Power is given by God, and the mighty will be strictly examined. Wisdom is easily found by those who love her.
7: Solomon says he was born like everyone else. He prayed, and wisdom came. She is a breath of God's power, a reflection of eternal light.
The New Testament uses this language for Christ.
8: Solomon loved wisdom and sought her as his bride. She teaches temperance, prudence, justice and fortitude.
The four cardinal virtues are named here.
9: "God of my fathers, give me the wisdom that sits by your throne." Who can know God's counsel unless he sends his Spirit from on high?
A model prayer for anyone with responsibility.
10: Wisdom protected Adam, Noah, Abraham, Lot, Jacob and Joseph, and led Israel out of Egypt.
God's wisdom has guided the whole story.
11: Israel was given water in the desert while Egypt's river turned to blood. "You love all things that exist; you spare all, because they are yours, O Lord, lover of souls."
God hates nothing he has made.
12: God judged even the Canaanites little by little, giving time to repent. "You have taught your people that the just must be kind."
God's power is shown in mercy.
13: People admired fire, wind and stars and took them for gods, when from the greatness and beauty of created things their Maker can be known.
A key text for knowing God by reason from creation.
14: A man prays to a piece of wood for a safe voyage. Idols began with grief and flattery and led to every kind of moral disorder.
15: "Even if we sin, we are yours." The potter makes a god from the same clay as a pot.
To know God is the root of immortality.
16: Egypt was tormented by creatures, while Israel received quail and manna, "bread from heaven, containing every delight".
The Church uses this line of the Eucharist.
17: The Egyptians, prisoners of darkness, were terrified by their own guilty consciences.
"Wickedness is a cowardly thing, condemned by its own witness."
18: Israel had light. "While gentle silence enveloped all things, your all-powerful Word leaped from heaven."
The liturgy applies this to Christmas night.
19: Creation itself was refashioned to serve God's children as they crossed the sea.
"In all things, O Lord, you have exalted your people."
